These bugs are infesting my kale! Help?

Is that an extreme zoom? They look like aphids to me, but they look so huge in your photo!

Cruciferous plants apparently get their own special breed of aphids...cabbage aphids. If just a few leaves are infected, pluck them off and toss them. That will control an outbreak if it's caught early. If it has spread, though, you can usually use a good jet of water from your hose to knock them off. I've also often used a spray bottle with water and some dish detergent to kill the aphids on my honeysuckles. Very safe treatment, and quite effective.

Yup dish detergent works like a charm.

Edit; you could also try ladybugs

I think it is, zoom, look at the wood grain. Definitely agree with what you said. I also find you can just squash them. Kill as many as you can and get that dish detergent water, also buying some lady bugs from amazon can do wonders.

So they're just a different breed of aphid? And yeah, it's a closeup picture.

They only seem to be on some of the smaller leaves; I'll try picking off the infected ones. If that's not enough I might introduce ladybugs as some others have suggested.

The only problem with lady bugs is that they do tend to fly....away. But it's certainly worth trying!

Make sure you check online for a picture of ladybug larvae. They look like something prehistoric. I killed a few on my plants before I realized what they were!
Yeah, I've heard that the larvae kill more pests than the grown ladybugs.

Look up a mix of chili pepper spray. My mom does it and it works well, she says. I prefer neem oil. Although I've been using it all summer and my aphid population in my greenhouse is...healthy. So I might not prefer neem oil.

I'm gonna order some ladybugs...

Tried ladybugs, they flew away; I probably didn't have enough. I'll try diluted detergent now. I've heard that a component of aspirin (salicylic acid) can stimulate the plant equivalent of an immune system, so I'll try that too.
rubbing alcohol in a spray bottle it will kill them on contact then wash the plant and repeat for a week or so to keep the eggs off.
